scenarios.description: real zero-config Bubble Tea v2 fixture, vanilla and instrumented builds, driven through PTYs with a deterministic 256-key burst

probeEventsPerFrame.reason: Bubble Tea exposes accepted View calls but not the pre-render event burst coalesced by its renderer.

bytesPerFrame.note: Actual canonical Go snapshot envelope bytes including the four-byte frame header.

fullSnapshots.note: Adapter debug counters across instrumented runs.

droppedEvents.note: Failed Go client publications; every failure emits its cumulative debug counter immediately.

coalescedEvents.reason: Bubble Tea owns renderer coalescing before the probe hook and exposes no counter for discarded View requests.

unknownFrameworkNodesPerFrame.note: Actual generic nodes in probe snapshots.

renderCorrelationRate.note: Latest driver-paired semantic revision divided by publications, summed per fresh session.

probeSerializationTime.note: Actual Go canonical snapshot plus wire-envelope encoding time.

parentNormalizationTime.reason: Charm publishes a normalized semantic snapshot directly; no parent semantic normalization stage runs.

parentProtocolValidationTime.reason: The live driver does not yet expose its decode/validation timer.

probeHotPathTime.reason: The E2E wall-time difference includes observation, IPC, PTY and driver work and cannot isolate the probe hot path.

applicationOverheadRatio.note: Ratio of median instrumented and vanilla 256-key burst wall times after one explicit warmup per arm; 1.0 means equal.

caveats: Wall-clock overhead includes the driver and PTY because that is the behaviour users experience in an instrumented test run.
Raw durations, execution order and paired ratios are retained so estimator stability is reviewable.
Unavailable values remain null with a reason; no zero is inferred from an unobservable framework counter.
